senses.sense_definition: Behavior exhibiting excessive, extreme, or uncontrollable emotion, such as fear, panic, or wild excitement.

examples.text: The unexpected news caused widespread <w>hysteria</w> and panic among the local residents.
She tried to stay calm, but her anxiety soon turned into pure <w>hysteria</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A psychological condition characterized by physical symptoms with no identifiable organic cause; conversion disorder.

examples.text: The patient experienced temporary paralysis that the doctors eventually attributed to <w>hysteria</w>.
Modern psychiatry often diagnoses cases of <w>hysteria</w> as conversion disorder or somatization.

traits.comment: superseded by terms like conversion disorder in modern medical practice

senses.sense_definition: A historical psychiatric diagnosis characterized by emotional excitability, sensory disturbances, and psychological distress without organic pathology.

examples.text: Early psychoanalysts focused heavily on the study and treatment of <w>hysteria</w> in adult patients.
The book explores how medical definitions of <w>hysteria</w> evolved over the nineteenth century.

senses.sense_definition: A historical medical disorder formerly thought to affect women and ascribed to disturbances of the uterus.

examples.text: Ancient medical treatises frequently attributed inexplicable symptoms in female patients to <w>hysteria</w>.
Physicians once believed that <w>hysteria</w> was caused by movement of the womb within the body.
